## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

*Sayings-Record of Chán Master Yuèlín Shīguān* — a one-juan Southern-Sòng *yǔlù* of **Yuèlín Shīguān** 月林師觀 (1143–1217), Línjì-Yángqí-sub-lineage master. Compiled by a group of nine attendant-disciples (*shìzhě* 侍者): [Fǎbǎo](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E5%AF%B6), [Fǎshú](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E7%92%B9), [Qìnghuì](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%B6%E6%9C%83), [Fǎqīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E6%B8%85), [Yǒuzōng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%89%E5%AE%97), [Wéiguī](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%83%9F%E7%8F%AA), [Dàoguǒ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E6%9E%9C), [Huìkāi](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E9%96%8B) (= Wúmén Huìkāi 無門慧開, the future compiler of the *Wú mén guān*!), and [Déxiù](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E7%A7%80).

One-juan Southern-Sòng Chán *yǔlù*, X69 n1354. Non-commentary; *commentedTextid* omitted.

**Huìkāi** 慧開 (1183–1260) is particularly noteworthy among the compilers: as *Wúmén Huìkāi* 無門慧開, he would later compile the famous **Wúmén guān** 無門關 (Japanese *Mumonkan*) in 1228 — one of the most important Chinese Chán *gōng'àn* collections. His presence here as a young attendant-editor of his master's *yǔlù* documents his early-career position.

Dating: *notBefore* c. 1150 (Shīguān's mature career); *notAfter* c. 1220 (shortly after his 1217 death).
